status_reason: Material (tablets), quantity (coating thickness) and location (pan coater) are known, so a provisional first assessment applies; the NIR + Raman result comes from a different coating process and is not yet proof for this coater.
answer: A combined probe is not yet shown to be needed. NIR + Raman gave the best result for pellet coating in a fluidized bed, and a combination counts only if its fused model beats the best single method on the same validation data. Test NIR alone with a diffuse-reflection probe first, then compare it with a combined NIR + Raman probe on the same tablets.

inline.headline: Test NIR diffuse-reflection probe for tablet coating thickness, compared against NIR + Raman in the lab before any in-line use
inline.probe: NIR diffuse-reflection probe for scattering solids
inline.install: Viewing port of the pan coater aimed at the tumbling tablet bed; exact position to be confirmed on site
inline.test_against: Combined NIR + Raman probe on the same spot
inline.not_final_because: The NIR + Raman evidence is for pellet coating in a fluidized bed, not tablets in a pan coater; the combination must beat the best single method on the same validation data; reference thickness must come from independent lab analysis; the NIR range runs to 2500 nm but the silica fiber covers only to 2400 nm; an endpoint stop needs validation before use.

problems.text: The NIR + Raman evidence is for pellet coating in a fluidized bed, and the feed-frame example measures blend potency, not coating thickness. Your pan coater is a different process, so NIR + Raman is a hypothesis to test here.
A combined probe is not shown to be needed. Combining methods helps only if the fused model beats the best single method on the same validation data.
Raman signal is weak and can be masked by fluorescence, so Raman may fail on coated tablets unless it is tested on your coating.

A thickness model needs reference thickness from independent lab analysis, not from the instrument's own calibration, and quantitative use needs models that are built, validated and then applied before an endpoint stop.

methods.why: Tablets are solid and scattering; NIR penetrates several millimetres, works with glass optics and remote fiber probes, and diffuse reflection suits powders and scattering media.
Best reported result for pellet coating in a fluidized bed; the two methods carry complementary chemical information and must beat the best single method here.
Adds molecular information complementary to NIR; the pharma example used 785 nm excitation, and the spectral axis is Raman shift in cm-1; signal is weak and fluorescence-prone.
Strong mid-IR absorption limits MIR to thin layers under 50 um, and ATR probes are described for liquids and elastic solids, not hard tablets.

questions.q: Does the coating contain a fluorescent or Raman-active component, and which dyes or pigments are in it?
questions.why: Fluorescence can mask Raman, and coating chemistry decides which method sees the layer.

questions.q: How is coating thickness measured today as a reference, and how many tablets with reference values per coating run can you supply?
questions.why: A calibration needs independent lab reference values across the thickness range.

questions.q: Is the tablet bed at the probe spot homogeneous, and where in the pan can a probe view the tablets?
questions.why: Same-spot sampling matters when the sample varies, and the viewing position sets the install.

questions.q: What coater temperature and probe distance apply, and what endpoint thickness and tolerance do you need?
questions.why: Temperature sets the fiber and probe build; the tolerance sets the go/no-go.

experiment.objective: Test whether NIR alone, Raman alone or fused NIR + Raman predicts coating thickness better, using independent lab reference thickness.
steps: Coat tablets in several runs spanning the thickness range and measure reference thickness on each tablet by independent lab analysis.
Record NIR diffuse-reflection and Raman spectra on the same tablets, using a combined probe on one spot (or time-synchronised separate probes if the spot is shown to be homogeneous).
Build PLS models for NIR alone, Raman alone and fused NIR + Raman (low-level fusion of synchronised spectra) on a calibration set.
Predict thickness on independent validation tablets from other runs and compare the errors of all three models on the same set.
Check the Raman fluorescence background on the coating and confirm the 785 nm excitation falls within the fiber range.
references: De Man, A, et al. (2024). Evaluating the improvement of blend potency measurements in the feed frame of a rotary tablet press using combined NIR and Raman spectroscopy. Analytical Chemistry, 96(26), 10586-10593.
experiment.go_no_go: criteria come from the client; the client must state the required thickness accuracy and endpoint tolerance

pathway.key_features: None measured yet; the key NIR and Raman bands for coating thickness are to be selected from the lab spectra.
pathway.path_reason: Key features and reference data do not exist yet, so the lab test comes first.

multispectral.why: NIR sees hydrogen bonds and polar groups while Raman sees the molecular backbone and non-polar groups, so their information is complementary.
multispectral.test: On the same independent validation tablets, the fused NIR + Raman PLS model must give a lower thickness error than the best single-method (NIR or Raman) model; otherwise use the single method.

assumptions: Tablets are solid and scattering, so a diffuse-reflection NIR probe is assumed (not stated by the client).
The pan coater has a viewing port or space for a probe (not stated by the client).
A reference thickness can be obtained for calibration tablets (not stated by the client).
